newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-MOLDOVAN PUTS GRASSHOPPER ON BRINK OF LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MOLDOVAN PUTS GRASSHOPPER ON BRINK OF LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Viorel Moldovan hit two first-half goals to fire Grasshopper to a 3-1 win over Auxerre on Wednesday which put the Swiss on the brink of a quarter-final place in the European Cup.
Grasshopper's Champions' League victory avenged a 1-0 loss to the French side two weeks ago and put the Zurich club top of group A.
The Swiss league's leading scorer with 14 goals, Moldovan's two strikes were his first in the Champions' League.

He put Grasshopper ahead in the 17th minute when he hammered home from point blank range past goalkeeper Lionel Charbonnier, who was left sprawling after making a diving save from Murat Yakin's header.
Grasshopper increased their lead when Kubilay Turkylimaz was brought down by Alain Goma and Moldovan scored from the spot in the 29th minute.
Auxerre cut the deficit when Grasshopper's Mats Gren scored an own goal just two minutes into the second half.
However, Grasshopper captain Gren atoned 12 minutes later when he rocketed a 20-metre shot past Charbonnier.
"We had to be very careful after Auxerre made it 2-1," said Grasshopper coach Christian Gross. "Obviously I was very relieved when Gren scored.
"This is not over. We still have some very difficult matches remaining. Glasgow (Rangers) can be very tough."

Weakened by injury, the French champions limped into a cold, inhospitable Hardturm stadium missing five key players including striker Thomas Deniaud, who scored the winning goal in the earlier meeting with Grasshopper and twice against Rangers.

"It's very disappointing that we're having these injuries at this point in the year when we're in the Champions' League," said Auxerre coach Guy Roux. "But every team has a string of bad luck at some point.
"We were eating cake early in the season and now we're paying for it.
"We didn't work hard enough in the first half. In the second half we did but it didn't go our way."

Grasshopper: 1-Pascal Zuberbueler, 3-Pascal Thueler, 4-Mats Gren, 6-Murat Yakin, 7-Antonio Esposito (Joel Magnin, 84), 9-Viorel Moldovan, 10-Massimo Lombardo (Harald Gamperle, 89), 11-Kubilay Turkyilmaz, 14-Johann Vogel (Alexandre Comisetti, 79), 28-Brent Haas, 29-Boris Smiljanic.

Auxerre: 1-Lionel Charbonnier, 2-Alain Goma, 6-Philippe Violeau, 8-Moussa Saib, 10-Antoine Sibierski, 11-Bernard Diomede (Abdelhafid Tasfaout, 71), 12-Taribo West, 13-Frederic Danjou, 14-Christian Henna, 17-Steve Marlet, 22-Eric Assati.
